Here's a fun fact about the word 'hello': It’s one of the most common greetings in English and dates back to the 19th century, when it was first used as an interjection in literature. The earliest known written example appears in Charles Dickens' "The Pickwick Papers" from 1836. Over time, it became a standard way to start conversations—especially over the telephone, where "Aloha" and other alternatives were also used. Fun fact: In some cultures, like Japan, people might say "Konnichiwa" (hello) instead, while in France, "Bonjour" is more common. But worldwide, "hello" remains a universal greeting!
